items.q: The interviewee does not mention 'The girl' directly; the term is used by the interviewer to refer to Ella Fitzgerald, whom the interviewee discusses in the third person.

ctx.x: We did a thing called "Mr. Paganini." (Inaudible) in this book, they don't ever do no thing like Mr. Paganini, but Ella could do those type of things -- (novelty inaudible) type of things.
She could do them good! And she put a style to them. She had a lot of talent. The girl had more talent --
And Chick hired her when he first heard her. He was telling everybody about it -- they thought he was crazy.

ctx.x: Because, you know, because after Chick was missing, we had to do a lot of things (inaudible) that went on in the band. We had to just turn around -- we wasn't going to do this, we're going to change this, we're going to change that, you know. Things like that. Wasn't much (inaudible) with Ella Fitzgerald. Ella would (inaudible). (inaudible) Come to a point where Ella is another attraction.

We had worked up to the point when she was a star. We had build -- like I told you before, we had started giving Ella pop -- (inaudible) Send her to make her pop. Send her straight pop with all the big pop songs. You remember I talked to you about that.
And her part -- we didn't have to do anything with her. She just stay where she was at. It was the band part we had to straighten out -- the opening.
